analysis.title: UBS Daily Consumer/Lux 29 Oct: ABI (+ve); Carlsberg (-ve); Campari (-ve); Henkel (+ve)
key_insights: FOMC held rates at 3.75-4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack preferring a 25bp hike. The Fed upgraded its activity assessment from 'solid' to 'strong'. Warsh was hawkish and pushed back on the idea that tech is insulated from monetary policy. Markets price about 21bp of hikes by December (~83% probability of one hike, down from >90%) and 70bp cumulative by October 2027.

After the US close, Nasdaq futures fell as much as 1% as Alphabet (-10% after-market) missed in Search, reviving AI cannibalisation concerns. MSFT (+2.9% after-market) beat on Azure growth of 48% (+3pts vs consensus). ORCL (+10% after-hours) rose after the CFO guided FCF positive in 2H28 and above $30bn in fiscal 2029 as capex declines.

Asia traded mixed on the split tech read-through: KOSPI lower as Samsung fell 5%, TAIEX -1.5% on hyperscaler capex guidance with no increase in the FY26/27 framework, China Semis -3%, Hong Kong Tech lower. Crude fell 1.4% (WTI $101.3, Brent $113.7). Iran proposals presented by Qatari mediators were reportedly unacceptable to Iranian officials.

ABI Q3 (UBS Buy): organic volumes +0.4% vs consensus +0.3%, led by Middle Americas volumes +7.3% vs +3.3% consensus, offset by Asia-Pacific -11.0%. Organic sales +4.9% vs +4.1% consensus, adj EPS $1.21 vs $1.15 consensus. Organic EBITDA +3.9% in line, but EBITDA margin of 36.1% missed 36.8% consensus. FY26 guidance unchanged. Shares up.

Carlsberg Q3 (UBS Buy): organic volume +0.3% vs +0.6% consensus on China volumes of -10% (destocking, subdued consumer demand). Organic sales +3.0% vs +2.6% consensus. FY26 organic operating profit growth guidance of 4-6% unchanged, with a ~DKK100m FX translation benefit now assumed. The Sept-Oct China exit rate is the key question.

Campari Q3 (UBS Buy): organic sales +3.4% in line with consensus, FY guidance reiterated. Europe +8% while North America -2%. UBS sees sell-out trends improving in North America and expects strategic initiatives to support accelerating organic growth in FY27. H2 is weaker than UBS expected.

Henkel Q3 pre-announcement (UBS Neutral): organic sales +6.5% vs +4.1% consensus (Price +5.4%, Volume +1.1%). FY26 group organic sales growth guidance raised to +3-4% from +1.5-3.5%. Adj EBIT margin guided to ~15.0%, narrowed from 14.5-16.0%. Adj EPS growth guided mid-single-digit.

Haleon (UBS house broker, Buy) Q3 organic sales growth +2.6% vs +3.2% consensus. FY26 organic sales growth guidance cut from 3-5% to around 2.5% on a Centrum OTC import suspension in China (50bps drag) and lower US Cold & Flu orders (40bps drag). New £0.5bn buyback. UBS cuts FY26/FY27 EPS by 1%/3%.

TMICC (UBS Buy) Q3 group organic sales growth +9.6% vs +4.6% consensus, with volume/mix +7.3% vs +2.8%. FY26 organic sales growth guidance raised to 5.5% from 3-5% (consensus +4.6%). Adj EBITDA margin improvement guidance of 40-60bps unchanged.

Japan Tobacco 3Q26 (UBS Buy) was broadly in line: EBIT +0.7% ahead of consensus, EPS missed by 3.4%. FY26 EPS guidance raised 2.8% to ¥373, DPS unchanged at ¥272 vs consensus ¥275. UBS sees scope for slight underperformance given recent share-price strength and the unchanged DPS guide.

adidas Q3 detail (UBS Neutral): Europe -4% cFX vs +2% consensus, attributed to conservative sell-in and an SAP migration shifting shipments into Q4. Footwear flat, apparel +19%, own stores +16%. FY26 EBIT guidance €2.5bn (€2.4bn ex tariff refunds). Q3 gross margin 54.3% (51.5% ex tariff refund). Management expects high-single-digit growth in Europe in Q4.

US consumer prints: O'Reilly Q3 EPS $0.97 vs $0.93 consensus, with about $0.93 ex a $39m one-time tariff refund. FY26 guidance raised to 5.5-6.5% comps and EPS $3.25-3.35. Sprouts Q3 SSS -0.9% vs +0.2% consensus with Q4 SSS guided -2% to -4%. Chefs' Warehouse had a third straight quarter of 10%+ organic sales growth. VF Corp Vans revenue fell 9.8% y/y.

China consumer read-throughs: Tsingtao Q3 net profit down 17.1% y/y with gross margin down 1.4ppt on raw material costs. Shanxi Fenjiu Q3 revenue -18.1% and net profit -34.5% y/y. Beijing Yanjing Q3 revenue +2.3% (a slight miss). Japan department store inbound duty-free sales rose 25.3% y/y in September despite mainland China arrivals down about 54% in Q3.

Previews: UBS is ahead of consensus on Henkel, CCEP, CCH, Diageo, Intercos and Richemont. UBS is below consensus on Ferrari and Hugo Boss. UBS is in line on Altria, Pandora and Burberry. Orkla is rated Sell with margin pressure building. Molson Coors Q3 preview expects underlying constant-currency EBT down 15-18%, with Americas organic sales -2% vs -1.2% consensus.

EssilorLuxottica: Leonardo Maria del Vecchio is reportedly weighing a €3.5bn offer to buy out his sibling's 12.5% stake in Delfin (Sole 24 Ore, via Bloomberg). Prada took #1 in the Lyst Index with Q3 demand up 55%.

market_movers.rationale: Anheuser-Busch InBev Q3 beat on sales and EPS with Middle Americas strength, offset by China weakness and an EBITDA margin miss. FY26 guidance unchanged.
Carlsberg Q3 volume missed on China volumes of -10%. Guidance unchanged. UBS flags the Sept-Oct exit rate as the key question.
Campari Q3 organic sales +3.4% in line. UBS sees Europe +8% and improving North America sell-out, and expects accelerating FY27 organic growth.
Henkel pre-announced organic sales +6.5% vs +4.1% consensus and raised FY26 group organic growth guidance to +3-4%.
Haleon Q3 organic sales missed and FY26 guidance was cut to around 2.5%. UBS cut FY26/FY27 EPS by 1%/3%. UBS is the house broker.
TMICC Q3 organic sales +9.6% vs +4.6% consensus. FY26 guidance raised to 5.5%.
Japan Tobacco 3Q26 in line with EBIT +0.7% ahead of consensus and FY26 EPS guide raised 2.8%. UBS sees scope for slight underperformance given the share-price run.
adidas Q3 detail showed Europe -4% and footwear flat, with FY26 EBIT guidance already raised on tariff refunds.
Q3 EPS $0.97 vs $0.93 consensus, though about $0.93 excluding a $39m tariff refund. FY26 guidance raised. PT based on about 32x CY27E EPS of $3.75.
Third straight quarter of 10%+ organic sales growth. PT raised to $135 from $125.
Q3 SSS of -0.9% vs +0.2% consensus and Q4 SSS guide of -2% to -4% raise questions on the return to the 2-4% SSS algorithm.
Mixed 2Q with stronger gross margin and EPS but Vans revenue down 9.8% y/y and unproven wholesale sell-through.
Q3 preview expects underlying constant-currency EBT down 15-18% with commodity and logistics headwinds above $130M. No near-term sentiment catalyst.
Q3 pre-announcement missed on the top line but beat on the bottom line. Shares are up 8.5% vs XLP since the print, which UBS attributes to positioning. Risk/reward balanced.
India-specific running shoe launch on 1 November as local expansion accelerates.
Ryan Lally promoted to chief brand communications officer.
Alexis Hoopes named chief merchandising officer, joining from eBay.
Watches of Switzerland nearly doubled its Glasgow Rolex boutique. The group runs 186 showrooms across the UK and US.
Tsingtao Q3 net profit fell 17.1% y/y on raw material costs and higher selling expenses while revenue was in line.
Shanxi Fenjiu Q3 revenue -18.1% and net profit -34.5% y/y with operating deleveraging.
Beijing Yanjing Q3 revenue +2.3% y/y was a slight miss, with margin expansion moderating.
EssilorLuxottica (Ray-Ban) rated Buy by UBS. Reported Delfin stake buyout offer by an heir of the founder.
Orkla Q3 preview (6 Nov) flags building margin pressures.
Unilever Q3 review: robust emerging markets quarter, but the upcoming MKC deal, necessary pricing actions and tough comps weigh on the name.

sector_views.rationale: Q3 results are mixed. ABI, TMICC and Henkel beat and raised guidance, while Carlsberg missed on China volumes, Haleon cut guidance and Campari was in line.
UBS is below consensus on Ferrari and Hugo Boss, in line on Pandora and Burberry, and ahead on Richemont. adidas Europe was weak, offset by strength elsewhere.
Campari sees Europe +8% while peers Pernod, Remy and Heineken reported underwhelming results. China cognac is described as fragile but improving.
Tsingtao and Fenjiu net profit missed on margin contraction, Yanjing revenue missed slightly, and Carlsberg and ABI saw China volumes down 10-11%.

earnings_insights: ABI Q3 (reported 10/29): organic sales +4.9% vs company-compiled consensus +4.1%, adj EPS $1.21 vs consensus $1.15, organic EBITDA +3.9% in line, EBITDA margin 36.1% vs consensus 36.8%.
Carlsberg Q3 (reported 10/29): organic volume +0.3% vs consensus +0.6%, organic sales +3.0% vs consensus +2.6%. FY26 organic operating profit growth guidance 4-6% unchanged vs 2026E consensus +5.5%.
Campari Q3 (reported 10/29): organic sales +3.4% in line with consensus. Europe +8%, North America -2%. FY guidance reiterated.

Henkel Q3 pre-announcement (10/29): group sales €5,713m vs consensus €5,575m, organic +6.5% vs consensus +4.1%. FY26 organic growth guide raised to +3-4% vs consensus +3.2%. Adj EPS growth guided mid-single-digit cFX.
Haleon Q3 (reported 10/29): organic sales growth +2.6% vs consensus +3.2%, vol/mix +0.5% vs consensus +1.3%. FY26 guidance cut from 3-5% to around 2.5%.
TMICC Q3 (reported 10/29): group organic sales growth +9.6% vs consensus +4.6%. FY26 guide raised to 5.5% vs consensus +4.6%.
MSFT FQ1 (reported 10/28 after the close): revenue $92.28bn (+2% vs consensus), EPS $4.92 (+4.5% vs consensus), Azure growth 48% vs 45.2% consensus, capex $39.37bn (-15.5% vs expectations).
Alphabet Q3 (reported 10/28 after the close): Search growth 11.8% vs 14-14.5% expected, YouTube +11% vs ~12%, operating income $41bn vs $44-45bn expected. Shares fell about 10% after-hours.
O'Reilly Q3 (reported): EPS $0.97 vs $0.93 consensus, comps +7.2%. Ex a $39m one-time tariff refund, EPS about $0.93. FY26 EPS guidance raised to $3.25-3.35.
Japan Tobacco 3Q26 (reported 10/29): EBIT +0.7% vs consensus, EPS missed consensus by 3.4%. FY26 EPS guide raised 2.8% to ¥373.
adidas Q3 (reported 10/29): sales €7,252m, +7% cFX, EBIT €1,008m (€808m ex tariff refund), both pre-released. FY26 EBIT guidance €2.5bn.
Molson Coors Q3 preview (UBS estimates, not yet reported): company guides underlying constant-currency EBT down 15-18% y/y. UBS expects Americas organic sales -2% vs consensus -1.2%.
Altria Q3 preview (29 Oct): UBS in line with consensus. A step-up in pricing could lead Altria to raise the low end of FY26 guidance.

macro_indicators.reading: 3.75-4.00%, held, 10-2 vote (Cook and Hammack favoured a 25bp hike)
macro_indicators.interpretation: The hold came with hawkish messaging. The Fed upgraded its activity assessment to 'strong'.
Hike pricing eased slightly after the meeting.
Longer-dated hike pricing fell despite hawkish rhetoric.
Crude eased from the prior day's highs with no new developments on Iran.
Visitor count rose 7% YoY but total sales growth turned negative.

macro_indicators.indicator: Japan department store inbound duty-free sales
macro_indicators.interpretation: Spending per Chinese visitor rose sharply despite weaker arrivals.

risk_factors: AI cannibalisation of Search after the Alphabet miss.
Hyperscaler capex guidance with no increase in the FY26/27 framework weighing on Asian tech.
China consumer weakness: destocking and subdued demand hitting Carlsberg and ABI volumes, and beer and baijiu margins.
Centrum OTC import suspension in China and lower US Cold & Flu orders hitting Haleon.
Tariffs: one-time tariff refunds inflating adidas and O'Reilly results, and H2 tariffs a headwind for VF Corp.
Commodity and logistics cost headwinds above $130M at Molson Coors, and raw material inflation turning in 2027 for BIC.
Middle East uncertainty affecting Chefs' Warehouse and crude prices.
vol_and_positioning: MSFT shares were +2.3% to +2.8% in the after-market session against ~4.7% implied move.
Nasdaq futures fell as much as 1% after the Alphabet miss.
Flow on Wednesday in Europe finished balanced (51/49). Industrials and healthcare finished better for sale, and semis saw demand.
Japan flat into the Topix rebalance.
geopolitical: US reached out to Iran on medical supplies, which is being downplayed. Proposals presented by Qatari mediators were reportedly unacceptable to Iranian officials.
UBS webinar on 3 Nov covers Iran tensions and the changing outlook for the Middle East.
Chefs' Warehouse cites Middle East uncertainty in its conservative Q4 guidance.
cross_bank_references: Campari: peers including Pernod, Remy and Heineken have reported underwhelming results in Europe (UBS commentary).

tension_points.bull_case: Microsoft beat on Azure growth of 48% with capex 15.5% below expectations, and Oracle guided FCF positive in 2H28 and above $30bn in fiscal 2029 as capex declines.
tension_points.bear_case: Alphabet missed on Search growth of 11.8% against a 14-14.5% bogey, reviving AI cannibalisation concerns. Asian tech fell on hyperscaler capex guidance showing no increase in the FY26/27 framework.

tension_points.bull_case: Hike pricing for December eased to about 83% from above 90%, and cumulative hikes by October 2027 priced lower than Tuesday.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed upgraded activity to 'strong', two members dissented for a hike, and Warsh was hawkish, saying tech is not insulated from rates.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS sees North America sell-out trends improving sequentially, helped by the Sarti Rosa roll-out, and strategic initiatives supporting FY27 organic growth acceleration.
tension_points.bear_case: North America Q3 was -2%, management was cautious on declining US brands (Wild Turkey, Skyy, Grand Marnier, Courvoisier), and H2 is weaker than UBS expected.
tension_points.what_invalidates: UBS's sell-out tracker showing the declining US brands getting sequentially worse.
